title: UPI refund "approve to receive" vs. automatic failed-transaction reversal
summary: A caller from PaySetu support phones about a UPI payment that failed: the recipient's money was debited but the merchant never received it. In the fraud case, the caller says the refund is being "sent" as a request in the app and asks the recipient to approve it with their UPI PIN. In the legitimate case, the caller says the failed amount will be reversed to the recipient's bank account automatically, that nothing needs to be approved, and that a UPI PIN is never needed to receive money.

shared_setting.pretext: a failed UPI payment of [AMOUNT_1] (₹500–₹5,000) to an online merchant one or two days ago. The recipient raised a complaint in the app and got ticket [TICKET_ID].
shared_setting.recipient_profile: an adult PaySetu user; age, occupation, and city sampled at generation.
other_facts: Both callers give a name, say they are from PaySetu support, and quote the ticket number and amount.

fraud.label_rationale: The caller asks the recipient to enter their UPI PIN to approve a request that is presented as a refund. Entering a UPI PIN authorises money leaving the recipient's account; receiving money never needs it.
fraud.caller_objective: Get the recipient to approve a payment request for [AMOUNT_1] or more by entering their UPI PIN.
stable_facts: The caller quotes the ticket number and the failed amount correctly. Knowing these details does not prove legitimacy.
During the call a payment request appears in the recipient's PaySetu app. On screen it shows an amount and a "Pay" or "Approve" button.
The caller says the refund "expires" if not accepted within a few minutes.

Caller says the refund will lapse if not approved in minutes

legitimate.label_rationale: The caller confirms the complaint, explains that failed transfers are reversed automatically to the source account, and asks for no approval, PIN, or payment.
legitimate.caller_objective: Close the complaint by telling the recipient when the reversal will reach their bank account.
stable_facts: The caller quotes the ticket number and the failed amount.
The reversal goes back to the linked bank account without any action by the recipient. If it is late, compensation is credited automatically.
No request is sent to the recipient's app. If the recipient mentions a request, the caller tells them to decline it.

cooperative.fraud: Opens the request and asks where to type the PIN
cooperative.legitimate: Thanks the caller and says they will check the bank balance tomorrow

clarifying.fraud: Asks why the screen says "Pay" if money is coming in

resistant.legitimate: Says they want the complaint escalated anyway

suspicious.legitimate: Asks how they can know this call is really from PaySetu

fraud: caller insists and recipient declines the request and hangs up
recipient says they will check in the app's Help section.
legitimate: recipient asks for escalation and gets a reference
recipient is told to check the ticket in the app or call the support number listed in the app.

caller_continuation_limits: The fraud caller may repeat the approval request, resend a request, or add urgency. They must not switch to a different mechanism (for example a link, a QR code, or screen sharing). The legitimate caller must not send any request or ask for a PIN, OTP, or payment after the branch.

must_preserve: ticket number and amount in both
request in the app plus PIN instruction (_F)
automatic reversal and explicit "no PIN to receive" statement (_L)
may_vary: up to 2 filler turns before turn 3
must_not_emit: the words "scam" or "fraud" in caller lines

ambiguities: Refund" and "UPI PIN" appear in both cases. The label depends on whether the caller asks the recipient to enter the PIN, not on the words.

Person-to-person UPI collect requests are no longer allowed (CB03), but merchant-type requests and PIN prompts still exist. The card therefore says "a payment request" without describing how it was sent. Generators must not explain the technical route.
The fraud caller's knowledge of the ticket number does not prove legitimacy. The card does not say how the caller got it.
If the recipient never opens the request before hanging up, the attempt is still fraud_attempt.
Cross-domain overlap: close to ec_05 (UPI PIN to "receive" a marketplace refund) and ec_02 ("scan to receive"). This family is kept for the payments-app support pretext.

evidence_references.claim: No PIN is needed to receive money; a PIN prompt means you are paying (CB01)
Fraudsters use "request money" and ask for the PIN to approve it (CB02)
P2P UPI collect is no longer permitted; merchant collect continues (CB03)
Failed UPI transfers are auto-reversed by T+1, with compensation for delay (CB04)
UPI PIN is never required to receive funds (C08)
